definition: Abate means to become less intense; to ease off.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Campers waited in the ranger station until the wind began to abate before rowing back across the lake.
A dip is milder than abating — a dip is a brief, shallow drop, while a force that abates is genuinely and steadily draining away.
Cease is stronger than abate — a storm that abates is still blowing, only less fiercely, but one that ceases has stopped altogether.

Subside means to sink to a quieter or lower level — floods subside, swelling subsides, an uproar subsides. Abate is about intensity easing off; subside is about a level dropping. A storm's fury abates, while the floodwater it leaves behind subsides.

Let up is the informal, everyday phrase for pressure or rain easing off, and it usually means a pause you can act in. Abate is the more formal word and points to a gradual, continuing decline in force, not just a momentary break.

Die down is the casual phrase for noise, wind, or excitement fading toward quiet, and it looks ahead to the finish. When a force abates, the word measures the easing itself — it may still be strong, just weaker than before it began to abate.

Abate means to become less intense; to ease off.
The protest noise outside the courthouse did not stop all at once; it abated through the afternoon, from chanting, to scattered shouts, to a murmur the clerks could ignore.
Abate is more precise than simply 'stop' because it names a gradual easing of force or intensity — the thing is still there, only weaker.
It is the word for winds, pain, noise, and anger that die down by degrees rather than ending in an instant.
Abate is the standard word in forecasts, medicine, and law for force that eases by degrees — storms, pain, noise, a nuisance.
In casual talk, 'let up' or 'die down' sounds more natural.
Note that unlike attenuate, which needs an agent doing the weakening, abate usually describes a thing easing on its own.
